#### 31. Room Gate Pro (`gate`)

*Category: Noise Removal & Restoration.*

A musical downward expander with a key-filtered detector, hysteresis, hold and
release. The **Threshold** percentage is the familiar main control: higher
percentages raise the threshold so the gate closes more readily.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Threshold | `0–100% (40)` | Gate threshold (higher % = higher threshold). | Raise it until room tone closes between phrases; lower it if quiet words get cut. Confirm the voice opens it reliably. |
| Range | `6.0–40.0 dB (20.0)` | How much the signal is attenuated when closed. | 6 dB is a gentle fade; 40 dB is near-silence. Check the noise floor on a pause. |
| Release | `40–400 ms (160)` | How fast the gate closes after the hold. | Short = abrupt, long = natural but lets noise linger. Listen to the end of a phrase. |
| Hold | `0–200 ms (40)` | Keeps the gate open after the level drops. | Increase it so gaps between words do not chop the voice. |

**Quick test:** speech + room tone → threshold until pauses close, range 20 dB,
hold 60 ms, release 160 ms: pauses are quiet, word gaps stay intact.

### DELAY, REVERB & SPATIAL

---

#### 32. Studio Reverb (`reverb`)

*Category: Delay, Reverb & Spatial.*

A Freeverb-style stereo room: eight feedback combs and four all-pass diffusers
per channel, with pre-delay, damping, wet/dry gains, tone shaping and width.
**Room Size** and **Reverberance** both feed the comb feedback, so together they
set how long the tail lasts.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Room Size | `0–100% (55)` | Scales the reverb tank's decay/size (averaged with Reverberance). | On a clap, raising it lengthens the tail; lowering it makes a small, tight room. |
| Pre-Delay | `0–200 ms (15)` | Gap between the dry sound and the reverb onset. | On speech, 0 ms fuses the reverb with the word; 60–120 ms creates a clear "room" before the tail. |
| Reverberance | `0–100% (60)` | Reverb decay amount (also feeds the comb feedback). | Raise it and the tail blooms; lower it and the reverb becomes short. Confirm it changes tail length, not just level. |
| HF Damping | `0–100% (50)` | Absorbs high frequencies in the tail (soft room). | High damping = dark, natural tail; low damping = bright/metallic. Compare on a cymbal/clap. |
| Tone Low | `0–100% (100)` | Low-frequency tone of the wet signal. | Lower it to remove low rumble from the tail; confirm the dry signal is unaffected. |
| Tone High | `0–100% (100)` | High-frequency tone of the wet signal. | Lower it to soften a bright reverb; at 100% the tail is unfiltered. |
| Wet Gain | `-24.0–6.0 dB (-6.0)` | Level of the reverb return. | Raise it for an obvious effect; lower it for subtle ambience. −24 dB is nearly dry. |
| Dry Gain | `-24.0–6.0 dB (0.0)` | Level of the original signal. | Pull it down for a wet-only sound; 0 dB keeps the dry level. |
| Stereo Width | `0–100% (100)` | Stereo spread of the tail. | 0% collapses the reverb to mono; 100% is wide. Check with headphones for a mono-compatible image. |
| Wet Only | `off/on (off)` | Mutes the dry path. | On = only the reverb tail. Use it to hear what the tank is doing, then turn it off. |

**Quick test:** a single clap → pre-delay 50 ms, size 70%, wet −6 dB: a clear
room tail after the clap; damp 80% darkens it, width 0% centers it.

---

#### 33. Multi-Echo Delay (`multidelay`)

*Category: Delay, Reverb & Spatial.*

A multi-tap delay with three behaviours: **Regular** (evenly spaced echoes),
**Bouncing Ball** (taps get progressively closer, like a bouncing ball), and
**Reverse Echo** (taps build up rather than decay). Each tap can change level and
time.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delay Type | `[Regular \| Bouncing Ball \| Reverse Echo] (Regular)` | Tap spacing pattern. | On a single clap: Regular is evenly spaced; Bouncing Ball accelerates; Reverse builds into the hit. Each must be clearly different. |
| Delay Time | `10–3000 ms (280)` | Base spacing between the first taps. | Short = slapback; long = distinct repeats. Tap along with a click track and confirm the spacing matches the label. |
| Time Change / Echo | `-200.0–200.0 ms (0.0)` | Change in spacing from one tap to the next. | Positive values spread taps apart; negative values bunch them together. Listen to the first three taps. |
| Level / Echo | `-24.0–1.0 dB (-6.0)` | Level change per successive tap. | −6 dB gives natural decay; positive values make later taps louder; −24 dB kills them quickly. |
| Echo Count | `1–30 (4)` | Number of taps. | Raise it and count the repeats; at 1 only one tap should sound. |

**Quick test:** clap → Regular, 300 ms, level −6 dB, count 4: four evenly spaced
decaying taps; switch to Bouncing Ball and hear the spacing shrink.

---

#### 34. Echo (`echo`)

*Category: Delay, Reverb & Spatial.*

A simple feedback echo: one delay line whose output is fed back into itself.
**Delay Time** sets the spacing and **Decay Factor** sets how much of each repeat
survives. Changing the delay time does not erase the echoes already in the
buffer.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delay Time | `10–5000 ms (400)` | Time between repeats. | On speech, 80–150 ms is slapback; 400–800 ms is a distinct echo. Count the repeats against a slow count. |
| Decay Factor | `1–95% (45)` | Feedback amount: how long the repeats last. | Low % = one or two repeats; 90% = a long trail. Confirm that high feedback does not run away into clipping. |

**Quick test:** single word → 400 ms / 45%: two or three audible repeats;
raise decay to 85% and hear the trail extend.

---

#### 35. Stereo Imaging (`stereoimg`)

*Category: Delay, Reverb & Spatial.*

Constant-power pan, mid/side width and channel operations (swap, mono, phase
invert). Use it to place a take in the stereo field, widen a mono source, or
check mono compatibility.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pan (L ↔ R) | `-100–100% (0)` | Constant-power pan from left to right. | Hard left at −100, center at 0, hard right at +100. Confirm the level stays roughly constant across the sweep (constant-power). |
| Stereo Width | `0–200% (100)` | Mid/side width: 0 = mono, 100 = original, 200 = extra wide. | 0% should collapse to mono (both channels identical); 200% widens. Check on headphones and then in mono for phase cancellation. |
| Channel Mode | `[Normal \| Swap L ↔ R \| Stereo to Mono \| Invert Both (180°) \| Invert Left Only \| Invert Right Only] (Normal)` | Routing/phase operations. | Swap should exchange sides; Mono should make L=R; Invert Both on a mono source should be inaudible (polarity flip only) but cancel against the original in a null test. |

**Quick test:** stereo music bed → width 0 then 200% (mono vs wide); pan full
left then right; then Invert One channel and confirm the center image collapses
on headphones (proof the phase control works).

---

### PITCH, SPEED & TIME

> These are offline transforms: they rewrite the selected region (or the whole
> take) when applied. Speech is the best test material because pitch and
> duration errors are obvious. Check that the processed region still lines up
> in time after applying.

---

#### 36. Change Pitch (`changepitch`)

*Category: Pitch, Speed & Time.*

WSOLA pitch shift that keeps the tempo: the signal is time-stretched and then
resampled back so the duration is unchanged. Semitones, cents and percent all
add together (100% ≈ +12 semitones, −50% ≈ −12). **Preserve Formants** keeps the
vocal tract character so a pitched-up voice does not sound like a chipmunk.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Semitones | `-24.0–24.0 (0.0)` | Coarse pitch shift. | Speak a steady vowel: +12 should be an octave up, −12 an octave down, with the same duration. Check a tuner or a reference tone. |
| Cents | `-100–100 (0)` | Fine pitch trim (100 cents = 1 semitone). | With a sustained tone, +50 cents should be a quarter-tone sharp; use a tuner to confirm. |
| Percent Change | `-50.0–100.0% (0.0)` | Alternative pitch amount (logarithmic): +100% = +12 st, −50% = −12 st. | Set +100% and −50% and confirm they match +12/−12 semitones. It should combine with the semitone control, not replace it. |
| Preserve Formants | `off/on (on)` | Keeps the vocal formants natural. | On: pitch-shifted speech still sounds like the same speaker. Off: obvious chipmunk/monster character. Compare at +7 st. |

**Quick test:** speech → +5 semitones with formants on: higher but natural and
the same length; turn formants off and hear the cartoon effect; then −5 and
confirm the duration is still unchanged.

---

#### 37. Change Tempo (`tempo`)

*Category: Pitch, Speed & Time.*

WSOLA time-stretch that changes duration while keeping pitch. You can set the
change as a percentage or as BPM from/to; **High-Quality Speech Mode** improves
the transient handling for spoken material.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Percent Change | `-75.0–300.0% (0.0)` | Speed of playback: negative = slower/longer, positive = faster/shorter. | +100% should roughly halve the duration, −50% should double it; pitch must stay the same. |
| BPM From | `30–300 (120)` | Source tempo for a musical calculation. | With BPM To fixed, changing From changes the resulting percentage. Confirm the displayed/effective change matches the ratio. |
| BPM To | `30–300 (120)` | Target tempo. | Set From 120 → To 90: the take should slow to 75% speed, pitch unchanged. |
| High-Quality Speech Mode | `off/on (on)` | Better transient/phase handling for speech. | On should sound smoother with fewer metallic artifacts; off is faster but more grainy. Compare on a plosive-heavy phrase. |

**Quick test:** 10 s speech → +50%: about 6.7 s and the same pitch; −50%: about
20 s; toggle HQ and compare the consonants.

---

#### 38. Change Speed and Pitch (`speedpitch`)

*Category: Pitch, Speed & Time.*

Varispeed: resampling that changes speed and pitch together, like playing a tape
faster or slower. Use it for creative speed changes; use Change Tempo or Change
Pitch when you need to move only one dimension.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Speed Multiplier | `0.25–4.0x (1.0x)` | Playback rate; pitch scales with it. | 2.0x = twice as fast and an octave up; 0.5x = half speed and an octave down. Confirm both happen together. |
| Percent Change | `-75.0–300.0% (0.0)` | Same control as a percentage: +100% = 2x, −50% = 0.5x. | +100% should match 2.0x; −50% should match 0.5x. |

**Quick test:** speech → 2.0x: short and high; 0.5x: long and low. Then use
Change Tempo at +100% and confirm the pitch does *not* change (that contrast is
the point of both effects).

---

#### 39. Sliding Stretch (`slidestretch`)

*Category: Pitch, Speed & Time.*

A time-varying WSOLA: the tempo and pitch ramp linearly from the start of the
region to the end. Use it for risers, slowdowns, or a gradual pitch drift.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Initial Tempo Change | `-75.0–300.0% (0.0)` | Tempo at the start of the region. | Set +100 → −50 and listen: the beginning is fast and the end is slow. |
| Final Tempo Change | `-75.0–300.0% (0.0)` | Tempo at the end. | The opposite of Initial; together they define the ramp direction. |
| Initial Pitch Shift | `-24.0–24.0 st (0.0)` | Pitch at the start. | Set +12 → 0 and hear the pitch fall over the region. |
| Final Pitch Shift | `-24.0–24.0 st (0.0)` | Pitch at the end. | Set 0 → −12 and hear it drop; confirm it is a smooth glide, not a step. |

**Quick test:** a sustained vowel → tempo 0%/0%, pitch +12 → −12: a smooth
downward glide with no clicks at the segment boundaries.

---

#### 40. Paulstretch (`paulstretch`)

*Category: Pitch, Speed & Time.*

Extreme ambient time-stretching: a large-window STFT keeps the spectral
amplitudes but randomizes the phases, producing a smeared, pad-like texture.
Use it on music or a single note, not on speech you need to understand.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stretch Factor | `1.5–100.0x (8.0x)` | How much longer the region becomes. | 2x is a mild smear; 10x+ turns a note into an ambient bed. Confirm the output length scales with the factor. |
| Time Resolution | `0.05–1.0 s (0.25 s)` | STFT window: shorter = more detail/transients, longer = smoother and more smeared. | Compare 0.05 s vs 1.0 s on a plucked note: short keeps more attack, long blurs it into a pad. |

**Quick test:** a single piano note or vowel → 8x, 0.25 s: a long ambient
tail; drop the resolution to 0.05 s and hear more of the original attack.

### DISTORTION, MODULATION & CREATIVE

---

#### 41. Distortion (`distort`)

*Category: Distortion, Modulation & Creative.*

An 11-curve waveshaper with drive, asymmetry, oversampling and a post low-pass.
The curves range from hard clipping to tube-like even harmonics; oversampling
reduces the aliasing that waveshaping creates.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Curve Type | `[Hard Clipping \| Soft Clipping (Tanh) \| Soft Overdrive \| Medium Overdrive \| Hard Overdrive \| Cubic Waveshaper \| Even Harmonics (Tube) \| Expand & Compress \| Leveller \| Rectifier \| Hard Limiter] (Soft Clipping (Tanh))` | Selects the transfer function. | On a 1 kHz sine, step through every curve: hard clip = square-ish, tanh = smooth, even harmonics = octave-rich/asymmetric, rectifier = buzzy octave, expander = dynamics weirdness. Each must be distinct. |
| Drive | `0–100% (45)` | How hard the signal is pushed into the curve. | Raise it: more saturation and harmonics. At 0% the curve should be nearly clean. |
| Asymmetry / DC | `-100–100% (0)` | Makes the positive/negative halves clip differently, adding even harmonics and potentially DC. | At +50% a sine becomes visibly asymmetric and sounds an octave-ish/richer; at the extremes check for DC offset on the waveform. |
| Clipping Level | `-24.0–0.0 dB (-3.0)` | Level at which the curve begins to saturate. | Lower it for more distortion at the same drive; raise it for a cleaner, more dynamic result. |
| Curve Parameter | `0–100% (50)` | Shape control for curves that use one (e.g. cubic/overdrive variants). | Some curves ignore it; on those that use it, sweep and listen for the knee/kink moving. |
| Oversampling | `[1x (Off) \| 2x \| 4x] (2x)` | Internal oversampling to suppress aliasing. | Feed a high sine (6–10 kHz) with heavy drive: 1x has gritty inharmonic aliases; 4x is cleaner. Compare the top end. |
| Post Tone LP | `800–18000 Hz (8000)` | Low-pass after the shaper. | Lower it to remove fizz/harshness; at 18 kHz the distortion is brightest. |

**Quick test:** 1 kHz sine → drive 80%, each curve in turn; then a 6 kHz sine
with drive 100% and compare 1x vs 4x oversampling (alias grit vs clean).

---

#### 42. Phaser (`phaser`)

*Category: Distortion, Modulation & Creative.*

2–24 cascaded all-pass stages swept by an LFO, with feedback, stereo phase and
dry/wet. More stages create more notches; feedback deepens them.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stages | `2–24 (6)` | Number of all-pass stages (notch density). | On pink noise, 2 stages = one broad sweep; 24 = many dense notches. Countable difference. |
| Dry/Wet | `0–100% (50)` | Blend of phased and dry signal (notch depth). | 0% = dry, 50% = classic phaser, 100% = all-pass only (no notches audible on its own). |
| LFO Rate | `0.05–10.0 Hz (0.6)` | Sweep speed. | Slow = 0.1 Hz (a slow whoosh); fast = 5–10 Hz (vibrato-like). Watch the sweep move. |
| Stereo Phase | `0–360° (90)` | Offset between left/right LFOs. | 0° = both channels sweep together (mono-ish); 90–180° gives a wide, swirling image on headphones. |
| Depth | `0–100% (70)` | How far the notches sweep. | 0% = static notches; 100% = full-range sweep. Check the extremes. |
| Feedback | `-95–95% (40)` | Feeds the output back into the all-pass chain, sharpening the notches. | Higher feedback = more resonant/whistly sweep; negative feedback shifts the character. Check that 95% does not run away. |
| Center Freq | `150–4000 Hz (800)` | Center of the sweep range. | Move it: the whole sweep shifts from low (vowel-like) to high (thin/airy). |

**Quick test:** pink noise → rate 0.5 Hz, depth 100%, stages 6 vs 24: hear the
notch count change; then set stereo phase 180° and listen on headphones for the
wide swirl.

---

#### 43. Chorus & Flanger (`chorus`)

*Category: Distortion, Modulation & Creative.*

A fractional-delay modulation effect with three modes: **Chorus** (thickening),
**Flanger** (jet-plane sweep) and **Doubler/ADT** (short doubling). Base delay,
depth, rate, feedback and mix shape it.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mode | `[Chorus \| Flanger \| Doubler (ADT)] (Chorus)` | Sets the delay range/character. | On a sustained tone: Chorus = lush detune; Flanger = pronounced whoosh; ADT = single short double. Each mode must be obvious. |
| Base Delay | `1.0–35.0 ms (15.0)` | Nominal delay before modulation. | Short delays flange; 15–25 ms chorus; 30–35 ms doubling. Listen for the comb-filter colour change. |
| Mod Depth | `0.1–10.0 ms (2.5)` | How far the delay is modulated. | Low depth = subtle shimmer; high depth = wide pitch wobble. Check that it does not sound out of tune. |
| LFO Rate | `0.05–8.0 Hz (0.8)` | Modulation speed. | Slow = drifting; fast = vibrato-ish. Compare 0.1 vs 6 Hz. |
| Feedback | `-90–90% (20)` | Delay feedback (resonance/ring). | Positive feedback intensifies the comb/whistle; negative changes the tone. High feedback should not self-oscillate into clipping. |
| Wet/Dry Mix | `0–100% (50)` | Blend of modulated and dry. | 0% = dry; 50% = classic; 100% = only the modulated copy (pitch wobble is obvious). |

**Quick test:** sustained vowel → Chorus 15 ms / 2.5 ms / 0.8 Hz: thicker;
switch to Flanger with feedback 60%: jet sweep; switch to ADT: one tight double.

---

#### 44. Tremolo (`tremolo`)

*Category: Distortion, Modulation & Creative.*

LFO amplitude modulation with five waveforms, depth, rate and stereo phase.
Unlike vibrato, tremolo changes level, not pitch.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waveform | `[Sine \| Triangle \| Sawtooth \| Inverse Sawtooth \| Square] (Sine)` | Shape of the level modulation. | On a steady tone: sine = smooth pulse; square = on/off chop; sawtooth = ramp. Each must be clearly different. |
| Depth | `0–100% (50)` | Amount of level modulation. | 0% = steady; 100% = full on/off. At 100% with square you should hear clear chopping. |
| Rate | `0.1–20.0 Hz (4.0)` | Modulation speed. | 0.5 Hz = slow swell; 10–20 Hz = fast flutter. Confirm pitch does not change (that would be vibrato). |
| Starting / Stereo Phase | `0–360° (0°)` | LFO phase / left-right offset. | 0° = both channels together; 180° = ping-pong on headphones. Check the image moves side to side. |

**Quick test:** 1 kHz sine → depth 100%, rate 2 Hz, square: clear chopping;
switch to sine: smooth; set phase 180° and hear the sides alternate.

---

#### 45. Wahwah (`wah`)

*Category: Distortion, Modulation & Creative.*

A swept resonant band-pass driven by an LFO and/or the input envelope
(auto-wah). It is the "talking" filter: the peak sweeps through the spectrum.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| LFO Rate | `0.1–6.0 Hz (1.5)` | Speed of the automatic sweep. | Slow = vowel-like sweeps; fast = wobble. Use a sustained tone to hear the peak move. |
| Depth | `0–100% (70)` | How far the filter sweeps. | 0% = fixed filter; 100% = full-range sweep. |
| Resonance (Q) | `0.5–10.0 (3.0)` | Sharpness of the resonant peak. | High Q = vocal/whistly peak; low Q = broad. Check high Q for a loud resonant whistle. |
| Freq Offset | `0–100% (30)` | Shifts the sweep range up/down. | Low = darker "ooh"; high = brighter "aah". Sweep it on a steady tone. |
| Stereo Phase | `0–360° (0°)` | LFO offset between channels. | 180° gives a wide, side-to-side wah on headphones. |
| Auto-Wah Env | `0–100% (0)` | How much the input envelope drives the filter instead of the LFO. | 0% = LFO only. Raise it and play/speak with varying loudness: louder input opens the filter. |
| Output Gain | `-18.0–12.0 dB (-6.0)` | Output trim (the filter can boost at resonance). | Match the bypassed level; raise it if the wah sounds quiet, lower it if the resonance is too loud. |

**Quick test:** sustained vowel → rate 1 Hz, depth 100%, Q 5: a clear "wah-wah"
sweep; set Auto-Wah 100% and stop the LFO by rate → the filter follows your
voice level.

---

#### 46. Vocoder (`vocoder`)

*Category: Distortion, Modulation & Creative.*

A multi-band vocoder: the voice (modulator) is split into 8–32 bands and each
band's envelope is imposed on an internal carrier. The result is the classic
robotic/talking-synth sound.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vocoder Bands | `8–32 (16)` | Number of analysis/synthesis bands. | 8 bands = very robotic and intelligible-ish; 32 = detailed and smoother. Countable difference on speech. |
| Carrier Type | `[Sawtooth Synth \| White Noise \| Original + Synth] (Sawtooth Synth)` | Timbre of the carrier. | Sawtooth = classic synth voice; White noise = whispery/breathy; Original + Synth = hybrid with more of the real voice. |
| Carrier Pitch | `50–400 Hz (110)` | Base pitch of the synth carrier. | Low = deep/buzzy; high = thin/robotic. On a sustained vowel the pitch of the robot voice should follow. |
| Noise Mix | `0–100% (15)` | Amount of noise added to the carrier. | More noise = breathier, less tonal. 0% = pure synth; 100% = whispered robot. |
| Envelope Speed | `1.0–120.0 ms (10.0)` | How fast band envelopes follow the voice. | Fast = crisp consonants; slow = smeared/pad-like. Compare on "ba ba ba". |

**Quick test:** speak "one two three" → 16 bands, sawtooth, pitch 110: robotic
but intelligible; raise bands to 32 (clearer) and envelope speed to 120 ms
(smeared).

---

### FADES & TIMELINE TOOLS

---

#### 47. Fade (`fade`)

*Category: Fades & Timeline Tools.*

Fade in, fade out, equal-power "studio" fade out (with a closing low-pass) and a
fully adjustable fade with start/end gains and a mid-fade boost.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Type | `[Fade In \| Fade Out \| Studio Fade Out \| Adjustable Fade] (Fade In)` | Direction/character of the fade. | On a steady tone: Fade In rises, Fade Out falls, Studio Fade Out falls and darkens, Adjustable follows your start/end gains. |
| Curve Shape | `[Linear \| Logarithmic \| Exponential \| Cosine \| S-Curve] (Linear)` | Shape of the fade envelope. | Linear = even; logarithmic/exponential = slower at one end; S-curve = gentle both ends. Compare on a 2 s fade. |
| Mid-Fade Boost | `-100–100% (0)` | Adds a bump (positive) or dip (negative) in the middle of an adjustable fade. | Only meaningful for Adjustable Fade. Set +50% and hear the level swell mid-fade; −50% and hear a dip. |
| Start Gain | `0–100% (0)` | Starting level for Adjustable Fade. | Set 50%: the fade starts half-level instead of silence. |
| End Gain | `0–100% (100)` | Ending level for Adjustable Fade. | Set 20%: the fade ends at 20% instead of silence. |
| Length | `1–100% (20)` | How much of the region the fade covers. | 10% = short fade at the edge; 100% = across the whole selection. Watch the waveform ramp length change. |

**Quick test:** steady tone → Fade In, length 50%: half the region ramps up;
switch curves and watch/listen to the shape; Studio Fade Out should also dull
the top end as it fades.

---

#### 48. Timeline Utility (`timeline`)

*Category: Fades & Timeline Tools.*

Three destructive timeline operations on the region: **Invert** (polarity flip),
**Reverse** (play backwards) and **Repeat** (loop the region N times). When the
action is still Invert and you change the repeat count, the effect honours the
repeat count automatically — the primary dial is never a dead control.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Action | `[Invert \| Reverse \| Repeat] (Invert)` | Operation to perform. | Invert alone is hard to hear on a single track (it flips the waveform vertically); Reverse turns speech backwards; Repeat loops it. Each must be obvious except Invert. |
| Number of Repeats | `1–50 (2)` | Number of copies used by Repeat (or honoured automatically if Invert is selected and the count is changed). | Set Repeat with 3: the region should play three times. With Invert selected and repeats 3, the take should also repeat three times. |

**Quick test:** a spoken word → Reverse: clearly backwards; Repeat 4: the word
loops four times; Invert: the waveform flips but the sound is unchanged (that is
correct — polarity is only audible against another copy).

---

#### 49. Truncate Silence (`truncsil`)

*Category: Fades & Timeline Tools.*

Finds silent spans (10 ms RMS windows) longer than a minimum and either truncates
them to a target length or compresses them to a percentage, with a short
crossfade at each splice. It is the "tighten the pauses" tool.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Threshold | `-80.0–-20.0 dB (-40.0)` | Level below which audio counts as silence. | Raise it and more quiet audio is treated as silence; lower it and only true silence is cut. Check on a noisy room. |
| Minimum Silence | `50–5000 ms (400)` | Shortest silence that gets processed. | Set 100 ms to shorten every gap; 1000 ms to leave short pauses alone. |
| Action | `[Truncate Detected Silence \| Compress Excess Silence] (Truncate Detected Silence)` | Truncate = cut each silence to the target; Compress = shorten by a percentage. | Truncate produces a fixed pause length; Compress keeps the pauses proportional. Compare on speech. |
| Truncate To | `10–2000 ms (150)` | Target length for Truncate mode. | Set 100 ms: pauses become short and uniform. Confirm speech is not cut. |
| Compress To | `5–90% (35)` | Percentage for Compress mode. | 35% keeps about a third of each pause; 90% barely changes it. |

**Quick test:** speech with long pauses → threshold −40, min 300 ms, Truncate to
150 ms: the take gets tighter with no clipped words; switch to Compress 35% and
compare the pause lengths.

---

#### 50. Spectral Edit (`spectraledit`)

*Category: Fades & Timeline Tools.*

An STFT-domain EQ: shape or remove a frequency band inside the spectrum. It is
the closest thing to Audacity's spectral selection tools — band-limited
changes that can be much sharper than a time-domain EQ.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mode | `[Spectral Parametric EQ \| Spectral Shelf \| Spectral Delete / Notch] (Spectral Parametric EQ)` | Boost/cut a band, shape a shelf, or delete the band. | On a chirp: Parametric = a local bump/dip; Shelf = one side shaped; Delete = the band disappears entirely. |
| Low Frequency | `20–20000 Hz (200)` | Lower edge of the band. | Sweep it on pink noise: the affected region moves. Ensure Low < High. |
| High Frequency | `20–20000 Hz (2000)` | Upper edge of the band. | Narrow the band and hear the edit become surgical; widen it for broad shaping. |
| Gain | `-36.0–24.0 dB (0.0)` | Boost/cut inside the band (ignored in Delete mode). | +12 dB boosts the band; −24 dB almost removes it; in Delete mode the band should vanish regardless of gain. |

**Quick test:** chirp → Delete mode, 2–4 kHz: that part of the sweep disappears
and the rest stays; switch to Parametric +12 dB and hear the band jump out.

---

### GENERATORS & ANALYZERS

---

#### 51. Audio Generator (`generator`)

*Category: Generators & Analyzers.*

Writes a test signal into the selected region (it overwrites, like a "Generate"
command): tone/chirp, noise, silence, a rhythm track, or DTMF digits. This is the
effect you use to build the test bench described in §2.

| Control | Range (default) | What it does | How to check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Generator | `[Tone & Chirp \| Noise \| Silence \| Rhythm Track \| DTMF] (Tone & Chirp)` | Signal family to generate. | Select a region and switch types: tone = steady pitch; noise = hiss; silence = flat; rhythm = beat; DTMF = phone tones. |
| Waveform | `[Sine / White \| Square / Pink \| Sawtooth / Brown \| Triangle / Blue \| No-Alias / Velvet] (Sine / White)` | Tone waveform (Tone & Chirp) or noise colour (Noise). | 1 kHz tone: sine is pure, square is buzzy, sawtooth bright, triangle soft. Noise: white is bright, pink balanced, brown dark. |
| Start Frequency | `20–20000 Hz (1000)` | Tone frequency, or chirp start. | Confirm with a tuner/spectrum: a 1 kHz setting should show/measure 1 kHz. |
| End Frequency | `20–20000 Hz (1000)` | Chirp end frequency. | Set 20 → 20000 (with a longer duration) and hear the sweep rise; set both equal for a steady tone. |
| Amplitude | `0–100% (50)` | Output level. | 0% = silence; 100% = full-scale (watch clipping). Keep test tones around 30–50% for headroom. |
| Duration | `0.1–600.0 s (5.0)` | Length of the generated signal. | Set 0.5 s vs 10 s and confirm the generated region length matches (clamped to the selection). |
| Tempo | `30–300 BPM (120)` | Rhythm-track tempo. | Tap along: 120 BPM = two beats per second; change to 60 and hear the spacing double. |
| DTMF Sequence | `0–999999999 (5)` | Digits played as DTMF tones in DTMF mode. | Try 123: three distinct phone tones in sequence. |

**Quick test:** select 3 s → Tone & Chirp, 20 Hz → 20 kHz, 3 s, 40%: a clean
sweep; switch to Noise / Pink for a 3 s pink-noise bed; switch to DTMF 123 and
confirm the tones.

## Appendix B — If it sounds wrong, check this first

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to check |
|---|---|---|
| A control changes nothing | Effect is bypassed, the value is at its default, or the control is a secondary/advanced one | Toggle Bypass → Enable; open **Show advanced controls**; confirm you are moving the right control; check another source that exposes that dimension |
| Output clips/distorts after a boost | Too much gain in one stage | Lower the effect's output/gain or add the Brickwall Limiter Pro at the end; keep peaks around −1 dBFS |
| Clicks when dragging a control | Coefficient stepping or a level jump | Sweep slowly; on EQs/filters expect smooth glides; note the exact control and value where it clicks |
| Everything sounds metallic after denoising | Over-aggressive spectral reduction | Lower Intensity/Noise Reduction, raise smoothing, re-learn the profile from a quieter noise-only region |
| Repeats/tail cut off | Effect has a tail but the selection/render ends | Leave silence after the sound; check the delay/reverb tail setting; on Apply, include the tail in the selection |
| Pitch/time effect sounds broken | WSOLA/stretch artifacts at extreme settings | Reduce the amount; enable High-Quality Speech Mode (Change Tempo) or Preserve Formants (Change Pitch); test on longer material |
| Fade/truncate does nothing | The selection is too short or the silence threshold is wrong | Select more audio; lower the silence threshold; check Minimum Silence |
| Ringing/whistling in a filter | High resonance/Q | Reduce Q (Wah, Notch), use a gentler slope (Classic/HPF), or lower Feedback (Phaser) |
| Noise gate chops words | Threshold too high / hold too short | Lower Threshold, raise Hold, increase Release |
| Effect applies to the wrong part | Selection vs whole take | Clear or set the waveform selection; Apply uses the selection when one exists |
| Values reset after reopening | Slot not saved / effect deleted | Confirm Apply or Done saves the rack; check the slot still exists |

## Appendix C — Automated parameter matrix per effect

Each effect id below has its own CI shard and a local runner. The command is:

```bash
FX_EFFECT=<id> sh ./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests '*FxParamMatrixDumpTest'
python3 tools/fxverify/analyze.py --cases app/build/fxverify/<id>
```

Effect ids (in rack categories):

- **EQ & Filters:** `hpf`, `highpass`, `lowpass`, `notch`, `shelf`, `eq6`, `geq`,
  `fcurve`, `basstreble`, `classic`, `tone`, `warmth`, `presence`
- **Dynamics & Mastering:** `amplify`, `normalize`, `loudness`, `dyncomp`, `comp`,
  `mbcomp`, `bricklim`, `limiter`, `gateexp`, `autoduck`, `deesssplit`
- **Noise Removal & Restoration:** `noise`, `specnr`, `declick`, `clipfix`,
  `repair`, `dehum`, `plosive`, `deess`, `gate`
- **Delay, Reverb & Spatial:** `reverb`, `multidelay`, `echo`, `stereoimg`
- **Pitch, Speed & Time:** `changepitch`, `tempo`, `speedpitch`, `slidestretch`,
  `paulstretch`
- **Distortion, Modulation & Creative:** `distort`, `phaser`, `chorus`, `tremolo`,
  `wah`, `vocoder`
- **Fades & Timeline Tools:** `fade`, `timeline`, `truncsil`, `spectraledit`
- **Generators & Analyzers:** `generator`

The matrix renders every parameter at min/default/max (every enum label and both
boolean states), against a probe chosen to expose that parameter, and compares it
to the dry render. Use it as the objective backstop to the listening checks in
this guide.

## Appendix D — 10-minute smoke test for the whole rack

1. Generate a 10 s pink-noise bed and a 10 s 1 kHz sine (Generator).
2. On pink noise, check the three EQs (`eq6`, `geq`, `fcurve`) and the filters
   (`hpf`, `highpass`, `lowpass`, `notch`, `shelf`) with one boost/cut each.
3. On speech, check `dyncomp`, `comp`, `gateexp`, `gate`, `deess`, and
   `loudness` at moderate settings; confirm bypass is transparent.
4. On a single clap, check `reverb`, `multidelay`, `echo` (tail, spacing,
   repeats) and `fade`/`timeline`/`truncsil`.
5. On a sustained vowel, check `chorus`, `phaser`, `tremolo`, `wah`, `vocoder`,
   `distort` (three curves + oversampling), `changepitch`, `tempo`,
   `speedpitch`, `slidestretch`, `paulstretch`.
6. On a noisy take, check `noise` and `specnr` (learn from a noise-only
   selection), `dehum`, `plosive`, `declick`, `clipfix`, `repair`.
7. Finally, stack a compressor → EQ → limiter and confirm rack order matters:
   swap the EQ and limiter and hear the difference.

If every step produces the change described in the tables above, and bypass is
transparent at defaults, the rack is healthy. Any deviation is a bug worth
writing down with: effect id, control, value, source, and expected vs actual.

the code. If you add or change a parameter, update the corresponding table and
the `tools/fxverify` matrix.*

================================================================================
TAKEONE — VERIFICATION BUG REPORT
Source: exhaustive FX verification harness (see tools/fxverify/README.md)
Run at HEAD 5f6c767 on branch verify/fx-matrix; fixes for the product bugs are
in the working tree/next commit (marked FIXED below with before/after numbers).
================================================================================


SECTION 1 — PRODUCT BUGS (audio engine)
================================================================================

BUG 1 — Chorus diverges into non-finite samples at high feedback        [FIXED]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Component : ChorusFlangerProcessor.processInPlace
Symptom   : At ch_fb = +90 % and -90 % the render becomes NaN/Inf. The DSP
            matrix counted 491,941 and 529,967 non-finite samples (of 576,000).
Root cause: Two feedback paths compound. The recursive state is one pole at
            fb (s[n] = delayed + fb*s[n-1]) and the ring writes back half the
            wet signal (ring = in + 0.5*fb*s[n]). Combined loop gain is
            0.5*fb*(1 + fb/(1-fb)), which exceeds 1 for fb > 2/3.
Fix       : Clamp the feedback coefficient to +-0.6 (loop gain 0.75 with
            margin) and recover a poisoned state instead of propagating it.
            Ring writes are also sanitized.
Before    : peak = non-finite (NaN), nonFinite = 491,941 / 529,967
After     : fb=+90 -> peak 1.93, nonFinite 0; fb=-90 -> peak 0.26, nonFinite 0
Bench     : 1 kHz tone 0.3, 12 s, 48 kHz, mono.

BUG 2 — Multi-Echo Delay feedback diverges (peak 5.76e11)                [FIXED]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Component : MultiDelayProcessor.processInPlace
Symptom   : md_level = +1 dB (its own max) with md_echoes = 30 produced a peak
            of 5.762e+11 on an impulse train — the repeats compound without
            bound.
Root cause: The delay line is the feedback path and the loop gain equals the
            sum of tap amplitudes (pow(levelLin, k)). Above 0 dB that sum
            exceeds unity and grows with the number of echoes.
Fix       : Keep the audible taps as requested, but attenuate the signal
            written back into the delay line so the loop gain stays at 0.9
            (ampSum > 0.9 -> scale 0.9/ampSum), and sanitize the stored samples.
Before    : peak = 5.762e+11
After     : peak = 0.935, nonFinite = 0
Bench     : impulses at 0.5 s / 3.5 s / ... , 12 s, 30 echoes, +1 dB.

BUG 3 — Multi-Echo Delay wet sum exceeds full scale at +1 dB             [FIXED]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Component : MultiDelayProcessor (tap summation)
Symptom   : Even with the loop stabilised, 30 taps at +1 dB sum to roughly
            +50 dB, so the wet signal alone exceeds full scale by >25 dB.
Root cause: The tap amplitudes are used as an unnormalised sum.
Fix       : Normalise the wet sum to unity when ampSum > 1 (decay shape kept).
            Defaults (level -6 dB, 5 echoes, ampSum ~0.97) are unchanged.
Before    : peak 26.7 (bounded but far above 0 dBFS)
After     : peak 0.93 with dry; taps keep their requested relative levels.

BUG 4 — Upward expansion boosts quiet material by the full ratio         [FIXED]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Component : CompressorProcessor (dyncomp_upward = true)
Symptom   : "Upward (Expand)" produced a peak of 2856 on a gaps probe: quiet
            material below the threshold was amplified by up to +40 dB.
Root cause: The gain sign was inverted for the expand path
            (targetGain = -slope * over, with over negative -> positive gain).
Fix       : targetGain = max(-60 dB, slope * over) so below-threshold material
            is attenuated, as expansion means.

BUG 5 — Auto make-up gain cancels upward expansion                      [FIXED]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Component : CompressorProcessor auto make-up
Symptom   : With dyncomp_makeup at its default (on), upward mode's attenuation
            was treated as "gain reduction" and compensated by up to +24 dB,
            boosting quiet passages back (residual peak 2.14 while the input
            peak was 0.30).
Root cause: Make-up gain is meaningful only for downward compression.
Fix       : Make-up is forced to 0 dB while upward mode is active.
After     : upward tone (-6 dB threshold, 20:1) -> out RMS 0.096 vs in 0.212,
            peak 0.136; gaps probe peak 0.136 (was 2.14/2856).

BUG 6 — Any diverging processor could poison the file with NaNs         [FIXED]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Component : FxRackChain.processInPlace (defence in depth)
Symptom   : A single NaN from any stage survives every later effect and reaches
            the preview, the bake and the encoder; the safety ceiling only runs
            when the legacy limiter is armed.
Fix       : After each processor's pass, non-finite samples in the buffer are
            replaced with silence. Finite audio is untouched bit-for-bit.

Regression test for bugs 1-5: app/src/test/java/com/example/hello/
FxDivergenceGuardTest.java (3 tests, renders each case to completion, asserts
finite and bounded output). Verified locally against the compiled classes and in
CI unit shards.

Measurements (before -> after), all with nonFinite = 0 afterwards:
  chorus +90 %           ~492k NaN/Inf -> peak 1.93
  chorus -90 %           ~530k NaN/Inf -> peak 0.26
  multidelay +1 dB/30x   peak 5.762e11 -> peak 0.935
  dyncomp upward         peak 2856     -> peak 0.136


SECTION 2 — OPEN PRODUCT QUESTIONS (not changed; needs a decision)
================================================================================

OPEN 1 — Multi-Echo Delay is loud at its defaults
     With default settings (level -6 dB, 5 echoes, feedback loop gain ~0.97)
     the wet signal rings up to ~2.24 peak from a 0.3 input, i.e. above 0 dBFS.
     This predates the fixes above and was left alone because changing it
     redesigns the effect's level structure. Options: cap the loop gain at 0.8
     for all levels, or scale output to the dry level.

OPEN 2 — De-Esser Pro (legacy stage) parameters did not reach the DSP when the
     rack was built programmatically. The app's own UI path is unaffected: the
     card's onSlotMutated calls cfg.syncLegacyFieldsFromSlots() before saving.
     The verification harness now does the same, but the fix has not yet been
     re-run through the device tier.

OPEN 3 — Filter Curve EQ (fcurve) exposes 61 of its 67 parameters only by
     dragging the curve canvas; only out/npts/taps are shown as pill controls.
     Parameters pf0..pf31, pg0..pg31 and npts are therefore unreachable from
     the advanced grid. This is a UI design gap, not a DSP fault.

OPEN 4 — AMR-NB container quality: decoded band error 14.9 dB (bands <= 3.5 kHz)
     against the 48 kHz source. Expected for a 12.2 kbps narrow-band codec, but
     worth stating in the app's own docs/limits.


SECTION 3 — HARNESS / OBSERVABILITY ISSUES (fixed in the harness, not product)
================================================================================

H1 — Three device shards hang their instrumentation (stereoimg, plosive,
     slidestretch): attempt output is empty and each attempt burns its full
     20 minute host timeout; the job is then cancelled at the 60 minute ceiling.
     Mitigation: the per-parameter test now has a 38 minute internal budget and
     writes partial results instead of hanging. Root cause still unknown.
H2 — Apply was declared failed while an offline render (WSOLA pitch/tempo) was
     still running: a 0.5 s wait was used for a multi-second render. Fixed with
     a latch that waits for the work (up to 120 s) and records the failure text.
H3 — WAV readers read bitsPerSample at the wrong buffer offset (byteRate's
     position) and rejected every fixture as "not a 32-bit float WAV". Fixed
     with absolute offsets; also accepts WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE float output
     from the runner's ffmpeg.
H4 — Emulator script lines run in separate shells, so shell variables did not
     survive between lines. Fixed by resolving paths per line.
H5 — The Add-Effect dialog could not be driven reliably (soft keyboard covered
     the filtered row); the rack is now cleared and populated through the same
     production config path, and every parameter's control is still driven in
     the expanded pill. Marked `addedThroughUi=false` in each result.
H6 — The screen recording froze behind a "Pixel Launcher isn't responding"
     dialog, so every screenshot was the same frame. Fixed by hiding system
     error dialogs and stopping the launcher in the device jobs.
H7 — Analyzer: an unchanged render was judged as "expectation not met"; anchor
     metric names missed the cmp. prefix; probe-derived series metrics were
     unreadable; anchors were matched across effects. All fixed; a self-test
     (tools/fxverify/selftest.py) now proves the analyzer can fail.
H8 — Renderers wrote >200 GB of intermediate WAVs per full matrix; compact mode
     keeps metrics plus failing renders only.

FILE: Takeone Admob And Paywall Removal.txt
=================================================================================
================================================================================
TAKEONE: POST-SAVE & SHARE AD FIXES, OFFLINE AD HANDLING & PORTRAIT-ONLY LOCK
================================================================================

1. POST-SAVE INTERSTITIAL AD FIX (`AdMobManager.java`, `StudioFragment.java`, `MainActivity.java`)
   - Root Cause 1 (`RecordingEngine.hasSession()` Race on Save):
     In `StudioFragment.runSaveDispatch()`, `AdMobManager.onTakeSaved(act)` ran
     on the UI thread while `ConversionJobs.dispatchSave(...)` was still starting
     on a background worker thread — meaning `RecordingEngine.get().hasSession()`
     was still `true` (with `engine.isSaving() == true`). `AdMobManager` previously
     checked `RecordingEngine.get().hasSession()` in `ShowingOrRecordingOrPlaying()`,
     which returned `true` on every save and blocked the post-save interstitial
     100% of the time (whereas during Export, `hasSession()` was `false`).
   - Root Cause 2 (`INTERSTITIAL_ACTION_INTERVAL = 2` & Transition Overlap):
     Having `INTERSTITIAL_ACTION_INTERVAL = 2` skipped odd-numbered actions, and
     launching `AdActivity` at the exact same millisecond as `act.exitStudio()`
     collided with the `STU -> LIB` FragmentTransaction.
   - Fix:
     * Replaced the post-save/export block check with `isActivelyCapturingOrPlaying()`
       (`engine.state == RecordingEngine.State.RECORDING && !engine.isSaving()`),
       allowing the post-save interstitial as soon as recording stops or enters
       the saving state.
     * Set `INTERSTITIAL_ACTION_INTERVAL = 1` with a 15-second anti-spam cooldown
       (`INTERSTITIAL_COOLDOWN_MS = 15_000L`) so every save, folder export, or
       share reliably triggers an interstitial.
     * Added a 350ms post-transition dispatch in `onTakeSaved()` so `exitStudio()`
       and the "Take saved" banner settle cleanly before `InterstitialAd.show()`
       launches, plus eager preloading when entering `StudioFragment` and a 4s
       late-load grace window (`maybeDeliverPendingInterstitial()`).

2. EXPORT -> SHARE INTERSTITIAL AD FIX (`LibraryFragment.java`, `AdMobManager.java`)
   - Root Cause:
     `LibraryFragment.shareFiles(List<Take>)` directly launched
     `Intent.createChooser(...)` without invoking `AdMobManager`.
   - Fix:
     * Added `AdMobManager.onShareRequested(Activity, Runnable onProceedToShare)`
       and wired `LibraryFragment.shareFiles(...)` through it.
     * When the user selects **Share** on the Export menu (single take,
       multi-select, or converting raw WAV share), if an interstitial is ready
       and eligible, it displays immediately and opens the Android Share sheet
       inside `onAdDismissedFullScreenContent()` as soon as the user closes the
       ad (or opens the Share sheet immediately if no ad is cached/eligible).

3. OFFLINE AD HANDLING, IN-MEMORY PRE-CACHING & AUTO-RECONNECT (`AdMobManager.java`)
   - Pre-caching in RAM while online (`preloadInterstitial()` on app launch and
     on `openStudio()`): cached `InterstitialAd` objects remain valid in memory
     for up to 1 hour (4 hours for `AppOpenAd`), so if a user goes offline or
     turns on Airplane Mode mid-recording, the preloaded post-save interstitial
     still displays when they save their take.
   - `ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback` (`registerNetworkReconnectCallback()`):
     Automatically initializes AdMob, reloads the `LibraryFragment` ad card, and
     preloads full-screen ads the instant internet reconnects.
   - Offline In-House Promo Card (`bindOfflineHouseAdFallback()`):
     When the device is offline and no live AdMob ad can be fetched, renders an
     in-house card in `libraryAdContainer` ("TakeOne Pro Studio • Coming Soon —
     Hardware mic switching & multi-channel editing") using `item_native_ad.xml`
     and swaps it for a live AdMob ad automatically once internet returns.

4. PORTRAIT-ONLY ORIENTATION LOCK & TELEPROMPTER STATE PRESERVATION
   (`AndroidManifest.xml`, `MainActivity.java`, `TeleprompterView.java`,
    `StudioFragment.java`, `layout-land/*.xml`)
   - Locked `MainActivity` to `android:screenOrientation="portrait"` and added
     `android:configChanges="orientation|screenSize|screenLayout|smallestScreenSize|keyboardHidden"`
     in `AndroidManifest.xml`, plus `setRequestedOrientation(SCREEN_ORIENTATION_PORTRAIT)`
     in `MainActivity.onCreate()`.
   - Unified `res/layout-land/activity_main.xml` and `res/layout-land/fragment_studio.xml`
     with the portrait layouts.
   - Updated `TeleprompterView.onSizeChanged()` and `StudioFragment.onSaveInstanceState()`
     to preserve `linePosition()`, `scrollOffset()`, and `telePaused` across any
     viewport resize or state recreation so the teleprompter never resets.

     /**
-     * Initializes the Google Mobile Ads SDK, enforces global ad audio muting
-     * so ads never disrupt microphone capture or audio focus, and preloads

+     * Checks whether the device currently has an active internet-capable network.

+    public boolean isNetworkAvailable() {
+        try {
+            ConnectivityManager cm = (ConnectivityManager)
+                    appCtx.getSystemService(Context.CONNECTIVITY_SERVICE);
+            if (cm == null) return false;
+            if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.M) {
+                Network nw = cm.getActiveNetwork();
+                if (nw == null) return false;
+                NetworkCapabilities caps = cm.getNetworkCapabilities(nw);
+                return caps != null && (caps.hasCapability(
+                        NetworkCapabilities.NET_CAPABILITY_INTERNET));
+            } else {
+                //noinspection deprecation
+                android.net.NetworkInfo info = cm.getActiveNetworkInfo();
+                //noinspection deprecation
+                return info != null && info.isConnected();
+            }
+        } catch (Throwable ignored) {
+            return false;
+        }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Registers a system network listener so if the app starts without internet,
+     * the moment Wi-Fi or mobile data connects, AdMob automatically initializes,
+     * preloads full-screen ads, and upgrades the offline house card in
+     * {@link LibraryFragment} to a live AdMob ad.
+     */
+    private synchronized void registerNetworkReconnectCallback() {
+        if (networkCallbackRegistered) return;
+        try {
+            ConnectivityManager cm = (ConnectivityManager)
+                    appCtx.getSystemService(Context.CONNECTIVITY_SERVICE);
+            if (cm == null) return;
+            if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.N) {
+                cm.registerDefaultNetworkCallback(
+                        new ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback() {
+                            @Override
+                            public void onAvailable(@NonNull Network network) {
+                                mainHandler.post(() -> onNetworkReconnected());
+                            }
+                        });
+                networkCallbackRegistered = true;
+            }
+        } catch (Throwable ignored) {}
+    }
+
+    private void onNetworkReconnected() {
+        if (!isAdsEnabled()) return;
+        if (!sdkInitialized && !sdkInitInProgress) {
+            init(appCtx);
+        } else {
+            preloadInterstitial();
+            preloadAppOpenAd();

package com.example.hello;

import com.google.android.gms.ads.AdError;
import com.google.android.gms.ads.AdListener;
import com.google.android.gms.ads.AdLoader;
import com.google.android.gms.ads.AdRequest;
import com.google.android.gms.ads.AdSize;
